claims.text: The material family is multiphase AlxCoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys with x approximately 1.5–2.0.
These alloys will undergo a ductile-brittle-ductile transition during aging.
The as-cast or homogenized alloy is initially ductile.
Aging for 30–100 h will make the alloy brittle.
Ductility will recover after more than 200 h of aging.
The non-monotonic ductility response is driven by the evolution of B2 long-range ordering and phase separation.
Strong B2 long-range order and coherent precipitates impede dislocation motion, increase critical resolved shear stress, and promote brittle fracture.
Prolonged aging coarsens the B2 phase, reduces coherency strain and LRO density, enables dislocation bypass or precipitate shearing, and restores ductility.
The initial microstructure consists of an FCC matrix containing fine B2-ordered precipitates.
The initial alloy has a grain size of approximately 10–50 μm.
The B2 phase initially has low long-range order.
Phase separation produces a Ni/Co/Al-rich B2 phase and an Fe/Cr-rich disordered phase.
At 500 °C, elongation will fall from approximately 20–30% to 5–10% at 30–100 h and recover to 15–20% at 200–500 h.
Yield strength will increase monotonically with aging time because of precipitation hardening.
The as-cast alloy has a yield strength of 600–800 MPa and elongation to failure of 20–30%.
The non-monotonic transition occurs only for x at least 1.5 because B2 ordering is significant in that composition range.
For x below 1.0, B2 ordering does not occur and ductility remains monotonic.
The transition is suppressed above 700 °C because of an order-disorder transition.
The transition is suppressed below 300 °C because diffusion is insufficient.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes the aging range as 300–600 °C, whereas the intervention and enumerated conditions begin at 400 °C.

The initial state is described as already containing B2-ordered precipitates but also as having low LRO in the B2 phase; this is ambiguous because B2 identification itself normally denotes appreciable chemical order.

The proposed long-time coarsening reduces coherency and obstacle density enough to restore dislocation motion, yet yield strength is predicted to increase monotonically through the same interval because of precipitation hardening. The hypothesis does not explain why overaging would not reduce strength.
